issue.title: Param Server - exception when using custom string parameter
issue.body:
I am trying to accomplish the following:
1) Have a parameter server (supposed to run on the OHD Ground station) for OHD related settings

2) test out the set / get -equivalents inside QOpenHD for then changing the settings.

So far I am just trying things out, but while doing so I stumpled across the following issue:

I add a custom (string) parameter to the server side:
https://github.com/OpenHD/Open.HD/blob/consti-test/OpenHD/ohd_telemetry/tests/test_mavsdk.cpp#L40

And just for testing, request all the parameters from the Ground controll application side: 
` auto result=paramOhdGround->get_all_params();`

Both the server and client side crash. On the server side, the output is:
```
test_mavsdk: /media/consti10/ade719d9-e80a-46da-8802-58ca3b8e08bc1/1_ohd-dev/MAVSDK/src/mavsdk/core/mavlink_parameters.cpp:1999: float mavsdk::MAVLinkParameters::ParamValue::get_4_float_bytes_bytewise() const: Assertion `false' failed.
[12:24:24|Error] Unknown type (mavlink_parameters.cpp:1998)
```

On the client side the output is less usefull:
```
See: https://mavsdk.mavlink.io/main/en/cpp/troubleshooting.html#user_callbacks
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::future_error'
  what():  std::future_error: No associated state
```

Any ideas ?

comments.body:
The issue above can be easily reprodcued by adding 2 lines of code to the autopilot_server example:

https://github.com/OpenHD/MAVSDK/commit/753f6553970fbda491fc66f4711a193dcce940db

Also, a question not a bug:

For commands or parameters set - aka stuff that is acknowledged - is there some type of re-transmission inside mavsdk ?

> For commands or parameters set - aka stuff that is acknowledged - is there some type of re-transmission inside mavsdk ?

Yes those are the [different](https://mavlink.io/en/services/command.html) [mavlink](https://mavlink.io/en/services/parameter.html) [microservices](https://mavlink.io/en/services/parameter_ext.html) :+1:.

> The issue above can be easily reprodcued by adding 2 lines of code to the autopilot_server example

Nice, thanks for sharing a reproducible example! This looks like a bug indeed. Would you be willing to look into debugging it inside MAVSDK?

> > For commands or parameters set - aka stuff that is acknowledged - is there some type of re-transmission inside mavsdk ?
> 
> Yes those are the [different](https://mavlink.io/en/services/command.html) [mavlink](https://mavlink.io/en/services/parameter.html) [microservices](https://mavlink.io/en/services/parameter_ext.html) +1.
> 
> > The issue above can be easily reprodcued by adding 2 lines of code to the autopilot_server example
> 
> Nice, thanks for sharing a reproducible example! This looks like a bug indeed. Would you be willing to look into debugging it inside MAVSDK?


Nice. I'l look into the source code more, still need to understand who/ what does the retransmission and how to change stuff like n of retransmissions usw.

Regarding the bug:

I've looked a bit into the source code. I don't fully understand it, but in short:

`paramServer.provide_param_custom("OHD_UART_NAME","/dev/ttyUSB0");`

is not a mavlink parameter but a mavlink extended parameter:
https://mavlink.io/en/services/parameter_ext.html

But for some reason the receiver calls 
` MAVLinkParameters::ParamValue::get_4_float_bytes_bytewise()`

on the extended parameter (which obviously is a string, not a float or int).

So 
` MAVLinkParameters::ParamValue::get_4_float_bytes_bytewise()`
should not be called - this switch is  probably messed up:
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/src/mavsdk/core/mavlink_parameters.cpp#L795

why - cannot tell yet ;)

So the issue seems to be created by the requesting side when calling:
`get_all_params();`

since when I explicitly request it using the custom keyword:
`get_param_custom("OHD_UART_NAME");`

It works. So when writing the implementation in mavsdk, the author did not consider that on a call to
`get_all_params()`

the server might provide mixed mavlink params and mavlink custom params.
I am not sure if mixing params and custom params into one plugin was a good idea ;)

Another thing, when looking at the code:
`get_all_params()`
would fetch all parameters (extended and non-extended).
But the imlementation only uses:
`mavlink_msg_param_request_list_pack`
and misses
`mavlink_msg_param_ext_request_list_pack`

So in theory get_all_params() should completely ignore extended params anyways ?
Honestly not completely sure. I'd say if the `param` plugin can automatically handle param vs param_ext, then that's better.

any idea how to run the tests under src/system_tests ?
The above should also be easily reproducable by extending the tests there.

Also, can you maybe get the person who wrote the param impl. into here ? I am a bit lost with exactly how things work in there.
found how to run them, jsut go into build/default/src/system_tests$

> Also, can you maybe get the person who wrote the param impl. into here ? I am a bit lost with exactly how things work in there.

@julianoes would know better, but he is on holiday at the moment, I believe :slightly_smiling_face:

thank you, I guess we have to wait then :/ I think the issue here is not easily fixable, at least for me. The more I read the code, the more worried I get how abstract the mavlink_parameters class actually is (aka what exactly can you use it for - to _**exchange configuration settings between MAVLink components**_ (which would be mavlink specification) or to _**exchange non-extended parameters between ground controll and PX4 FC and extended parameters between ground controll and a camera component**_

Because I read comments like 
`// FIXME: extended currently always go to the camera component`
and
`MAV_COMP_ID_AUTOPILOT1); // FIXME: what should the component be?
`

which makes me worried if we can even use mavsdk "parameters" for our intended purpose
(exchange non-extended and extended parameters between mavlink components)

> which makes me worried if we can even use mavsdk "parameters" for our intended purpose
(exchange non-extended and extended parameters between mavlink components)

The functions to set params (e.g. `set_param_int`) take a component id and a boolean telling them if it should use the extended microservice or not:

```c++
MAVLinkParameters::Result SystemImpl::set_param_int(
    const std::string& name,
    int32_t value,
    std::optional<uint8_t> maybe_component_id,
    bool extended)
{
    return _params.set_param_int(name, value, maybe_component_id, extended);
}
```

So it is possible at the lower level. Maybe even from the MavlinkPassthrough plugin.

Now the question is the interface: should the param plugin allow you to set the component id, or should the component id be abstracted away by MAVSDK? My intuition would be that it should be abstracted away. For instance, the camera plugin uses the params under the hood, but exposed as camera settings.

So somehow the param plugin talks to the autopilot, and the param server maybe should represent an autopilot? Then the camera plugin talks to a camera, and the camera server uses params under the hood, but not directly the params server.

What do you think?

Yeah, so the `set_xxx` take extended as a param, but that alone doesn't really help. 

I am pretty sure I now understand how the issue arrises (not 100% sure):

1) The server gets a get_all request (non-extended)
-> it then needs to respond with all the parameters 
-> it does so by just taking all the parameters it stores and sending them out as PARAM_VALUE

But oops, since the server has a parameter which is std:.string of type and non-ext cannot handle strings it fails.

This exact issue can then be mitigated by just making sure the server ignores parameters that do not fit into non-ext messages.

And when I do that in code, at least the server doesn't crash anymore as described above.

But now we've made the param class even more complicated .

Which then brings us back to the original question weather one should mix non-ext and ext ;)

My Opinion is the following:

1) A mavlink parameter server (or provider) is defined easily:
a) Store settings
b) allow changing settings (parameters) when requested by another mavlink system
c) provide current state of parameters to other mavlink systems when requested
d) notify the program (itself) of changes in the stored settings 

Now in theory, it would be possible to implement the param server that it works both with non-ext and ext messages - but then one would have to make sure that internally stored parameters that only work on extended (aka strings) only make it out to requesting components that speak extended (and then need to speak extended exclusively).

Which makes an already really complex class like MAVLinkParameters even more complex ;). 
(and I fear that only fixing the bug as described above is not the only one).


R.n I don't really have a solution for all these issues/bugs - or at least not a solution that doesn't require like >20h of programming ;).

But on a side note, I noticed the complete lack of documentation in the code under src/core/mavlink_parameters.h.c . Is there an internal documentation that is not published or is there simply no documentation at all ?

A cuple of updates:
1) I found the reason for the client side crash - this one is a simple fix, the all_params callback takes a reference but this reference can go out of scope, resulting in a crash.

2) With the fix I proposed before, the get_all_params() now doesn't work anymore if there are parameters that need the ext. protocoll - the class would have to track the count of parameters seperatively for ext and non-ext.
Oh nice! Could you open a PR with your fix for 1? That's already worth it, right?

Sure, I'd love to talk to the author though, these changes might have implications one cannot see immediately.

get_all_params() is now working again, but obviosly only returns parameters that do not neccessarily need the extended protocoll.

Ideally, we'l have 
get_all_params_non_extended() and
get_all_params_extended() soon.
Interesting, I will have a closer look next week.

I've been working on mavlink_parameters for the last couple of days. My goal has been to reduce the amount of duplicated code,without reducing the public functionalities (which are thought out quite well). 

So far, I have found a ton of cases where by just using templates or similar the duplicated code collapses nicely.

The only one's that are missing so far are the set_param_xxx methods from the non-servier (client side), which are extra tricky due to the  `// We need to know the exact int type first.` part

> The only one's that are missing so far are the set_param_xxx methods from the non-servier (client side), which are extra tricky due to the // We need to know the exact int type first. part

Exactly, that's where it gets tricky.

Uh oh, I hope you built on top of my refactoring!?

https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/1772
Oh dang, no, I did not know such a task is already underway - I totally agree though, splitting them into 2 is a really good idea.
Having a quick glance at it, one of the steps we both did is to extrakt ParamValue out ;) nice to see we are on the same page then.

And looking into your pull request, merging the 2 branches directly probably won't work, but especially since recv/ server are now split I think it would be easy for me to just copy stuff over and create a new pull request based on your pr request. Then I also have to think a bit more about my commit messages ;)

Do you have any local changes in regard to parameters or is this pull request still up to date ?

One more thing I'd like to put out for discussion:

Should the server-side make sure that parameter's types are immutable ?

For example, when the client sends a [PARAM_SET](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#PARAM_SET) message, but the type of the message doesn't match the internally stored type, what does the server do ?

In my opininion, the server should then ignore the update and respond with a PARAM_VALUE with the unchanged type & value for non-extended and a [PARAM_EXT_ACK](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#PARAM_EXT_ACK) with error code set in case of extended.

Unfortunately, the mavlink specification doesn't give out a quideline here, but I'd think that this is a fair restrictive quide line.

> And looking into your pull request, merging the 2 branches directly probably won't work, but especially since recv/ server are now split I think it would be easy for me to just copy stuff over and create a new pull request based on your pr request. Then I also have to think a bit more about my commit messages ;)
> 
> Do you have any local changes in regard to parameters or is this pull request still up to date ?

Please let me know soon, r.n I still have all the changes in my head and could easily just manually copy them over.

> Do you have any local changes in regard to parameters or is this pull request still up to date ?

No, that's all pushed.

> For example, when the client sends a [PARAM_SET](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#PARAM_SET) message, but the type of the message doesn't match the internally stored type, what does the server do ?

Hmm. The problem is that there is no "nack type error" for that case. So according to [the docs](https://mavlink.io/en/services/parameter.html#write) it says:

> The Drone must acknowledge the PARAM_SET by broadcasting a PARAM_VALUE even if the write operation fails. In this case the PARAM_VALUE will be the current/unchanged parameter value.

> In my opininion, the server should then ignore the update and respond with a PARAM_VALUE with the unchanged type & value for non-extended and a [PARAM_EXT_ACK](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#PARAM_EXT_ACK) with error code set in case of extended.

Ah yes, what you said :smile:.

> 
> No, that's all pushed.
>

>

> 
> > The Drone must acknowledge the PARAM_SET by broadcasting a PARAM_VALUE even if the write operation fails. In this case the PARAM_VALUE will be the current/unchanged parameter value.

> > In my opininion, the server should then ignore the update and respond with a PARAM_VALUE with the unchanged type & value for non-extended and a [PARAM_EXT_ACK](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#PARAM_EXT_ACK) with error code set in case of extended.
> 
> Ah yes, what you said smile.

Thanks for letting me know. I'l see if I can merge it today then.

Regarding the nack type error:
I am asking because right now the behaviour is to overwrite the value  type:
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/pr-split-mavlink-params/src/mavsdk/core/mavlink_parameter_receiver.cpp#L167

@julianoes 

I am mostly done with the param providing part (mavlink_parameter_receiver.cc / .h )
https://github.com/OpenHD/MAVSDK/blob/b3d9651391d888d949274095baa1f6ee5e7a4115/src/mavsdk/core/mavlink_parameter_receiver.h

There are 2 TODO's left -
1) what to do if the value to set matches the current value (for examle, provider currently has value x=1.0 and gets a reques to change x to 1.0 ) - what response do we send in this case and do we call the listeners
2) currently, using indices instead of the name strings as ID's is unsupported, even though in the mavlink specification
(Request the value of a specific parameter using **EITHER** its param_id or param_index )




Next up is the requesting / mavlink_parameter_sender.cc / .h part, this one is a bit more complicated. But I should be done in the next coule of days.
I believe this has been fixed.

repository.description: API and library for MAVLink compatible systems written in C++ 20

issue.body:
Opening this pull request to show the fixes, **not ready to be merged yet.**.

Related to https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/issues/1805

Fixes for mavlink_param when used as 
1) Server:
Do not forward parameters that need extended protocoll (string-values) on non-ext param requests, this made the original impl crash at run time.

The fix I went with seems to work but is not the nicest in my opinion - I basically try and hide parameters that only work with extended from a non-extended perspective.

2) Client:
Fix bug where reference goes out of scope, which resulted in the client crashing.

> Hmm. The problem is that there is no "nack type error" for that case. So according to [the docs](https://mavlink.io/en/services/parameter.html#write) it says:
> 
> > The Drone must acknowledge the PARAM_SET by broadcasting a PARAM_VALUE even if the write operation fails. In this case the PARAM_VALUE will be the current/unchanged parameter value.
> 
> > In my opininion, the server should then ignore the update and respond with a PARAM_VALUE with the unchanged type & value for non-extended and a [PARAM_EXT_ACK](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#PARAM_EXT_ACK) with error code set in case of extended.
> 
> Ah yes, what you said smile.

Thanks for letting me know. I'l see if I can merge it today then.

Regarding the nack type error:
I am asking because right now the behaviour is to overwrite the value  type:
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/pr-split-mavlink-params/src/mavsdk/core/mavlink_parameter_receiver.cpp#L167

repository.name: MAVSDK
repository.description: API and library for MAVLink compatible systems written in C++ 20

issue.body:
This builds up on the work already done by @julianoes in https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/1772

And replaces this pull request:
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/1807

Goals:
Refactor mavlink parameters to reduce duplicated code, eliminate bugs(relates to https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/issues/1805) and document the code without changing the public api's.

In general, the work flow for refactoring is:
1) Implement a generic way (for example a templated `retrieve_server_param` ) method
2) refactor the fixed type methods (for example `retrieve_server_param_float, retrieve_server_param_int, ...`

Not all of the refactorings are that simple, but in general the workflow is the same.

issue.title: get all parameters doesn't update values

repository.name: WayWise
repository.description: A rapid prototyping library for connected, autonomous vehicles developed at RISE Dependable Transport Systems

issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
Param::AllParams mavsdk::Param::get_all_params() doesn't retreive the updated values, but requests on specific parameter values with for example std::pair<Result, int32_t> get_param_int(std::string name) does.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Open ControlTower and RCCar
2. Click on 'Vehicle Parameters' and then 'Get Parameters From Vehicle'. Change a value and then click 'Set New...'. If you now click 'Get Param...' the list will update and your newly set value will return to old value

**Expected behavior**
Clicking 'Get Parameter...' should display the current values, including your newly changed one

**Screenshots**
![Screenshot from 2024-02-01 11-23-53](https://github.com/RISE-Dependable-Transport-Systems/WayWise/assets/76961018/e74955ed-10d1-44e9-ab10-2a99b40d6798)


**System (please complete the following information):**
 - Hardware: [Desktop]
 - OS: [Ubuntu Linux]
 - Version [22.04]

**Additional context**
Seems MAVSDK has had problems with the Param::AllParams mavsdk::Param::get_all_params() function for quite some time 
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/issues/1805
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/issues/2100

There has also been a refactoring lately
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/1772

I made a temporary fix that's to be removed when this is resolved
https://github.com/RISE-Dependable-Transport-Systems/WayWise/commit/636d308a02d03c340fc8761ebfac627d44127961
